thread:
Ravi P.: FYI getting alerts: apac-ingress showing elevated mTLS failures since 02:03 JST. Roughly 30% of client hellos missing expected cert selection.
Marta L.: I see it too. Error pattern: downstream services reporting keystore lookup -> fail -> fallback cert used -> mTLS mismatch. Sample log: `WARN keystore: key_lookup fallback_key_id=projects/.../cryptoKeys/alias-prod-legacy`
Omar J.: We rolled PR #4521 yesterday that tightened KMS decrypt scoping (policy: restrict-kms-decrypt-svc). Could be related.
Ravi P.: Correlating kc audit: many `projects/.../cryptoKeys/alias-prod-legacy:Decrypt` showing DENIED for principal=svc-ingress.apac. Time window matches.
security-bot: :rotating_light: Alert 3781239999: mtls_handshake_error rate increased (apac). Traces attached: https://internal/alerts/3781239999
Marta L.: Quick mitigation: add local keystore fallback mapping so svc-ingress doesn't call KMS for legacy alias. I'll push a hotpatch config to use cached key material if available.
Omar J.: Also, rolling back the RBAC change for svc-ingress might be faster. Which principal was scoped down? Looks like we removed `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` for svc-ingress to limit blast radius.
Ravi P.: Rollback approved. Omar, can you revert the role binding? Command: `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod --member=serviceAccount:svc-ingress@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter --condition=None`
deploy-bot: deploy started for ingress-keystore-hotpatch (canary apac-1). Link: https://ci/deploy/8899
Marta L.: Hotpatch applied to canary and handshake errors dropped ~70% in apac-canary. Getting ready to roll to apac-1/2.
Ravi P.: KMS audit tail: `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="Decrypt" AND resource.labels.key_id:alias-prod-legacy' --freshness=2h` shows DENIED -> ACCEPT after rollback.
security-bot: incident SEC-2026-220 created: apac-keystore-rbac-regression. Assigned eng-security.
Omar J.: Root cause hypothesis: RBAC scoping removed decrypt permission for service principal that still needed it for legacy alias used when SNI is missing or when client requested default route. Two problems combined: (1) RBAC change deployed without canary, (2) forwarders in apac sometimes strip SNI for special tenants.
Marta L.: Action items: 1) revert RBAC change and run canary RBAC rollout with smoke decrypt checks, 2) add integration test that verifies keystore.decrypt succeeds for all service principals in apac region, 3) adjust forwarder config to preserve SNI by default and only set preserve_sni:false for specific tenant through per-tenant config, 4) add monitoring alert for `kms.decrypt:DENIED` spikes tagged by principal.
Ravi P.: Also set temporary elevated audit retention for keystore and proxy logs and export to our sec-audit-bucket for postmortem. Command: `gsutil cp $(gcloud logging read ... ) gs://sec-audit-bucket/incidents/3781239999/`
Omar J.: I'll open a PR with canary RBAC rollout plan and smoke test scripts. Marking as P0 for next 48hrs.
Marta L.: Noted one oddity: a small set of client IPs had missing SNI but used a hostname header that mapped to a different backend. We'll add a validation gate in forwarders to log SNI/Host mismatches.
security-bot: summary: incident SEC-2026-220 escalated -> rollback applied -> monitoring shows recovery.
Ravi P.: Thanks team. Keep thread updates brief. We'll convert this into a postmortem after 72h when logs fully ingested.
